reference: Pinedo, Michael. "Scheduling: Theory, Algorithms, and Systems." Springer, 5th edition (2016).
math_formula:
### Mathematical Model
A permutation flow shop has jobs J, shared sequence positions K with |K|=|J|, and machines M arranged in a fixed processing order. Parameter p[j,m] is the processing time of job j on machine m. Binary variable x[j,k] equals 1 when job j is assigned to shared sequence position k; this assignment is not machine-specific, so every machine follows the same permutation. Start-time variable t[k,m] is the start time of the job in position k on machine m, and Cmax is the explicit makespan variable. Minimize Cmax. Constraints enforce one job per position, one position per job, machine-stage precedence t[k,m+1] >= t[k,m] + sum_j p[j,m] x[j,k], same-machine ordering between adjacent shared positions t[k+1,m] >= t[k,m] + sum_j p[j,m] x[j,k], and the final completion bound Cmax >= t[last_position,last_machine] + sum_j p[j,last_machine] x[j,last_position]. The p[j,last_machine] coefficients in the bound are final-machine processing times, not assignment costs or delay weights.
natural_language_example: A production line must process several jobs through the same ordered set of machines. Every job visits every machine in that fixed machine order, but processing times differ by job and machine. The planner chooses one common job sequence shared by all machines and computes start times for each shared sequence position on each machine. A job cannot start its next machine before finishing the previous one, and a machine cannot process two adjacent sequence positions at the same time. The objective is to minimize the makespan: the completion time of the job assigned to the final shared sequence position on the final machine.
local_modification_notes: Internal OR-CPT version records the permutation-flow-shop structure, exposes job-machine processing tables, uses an explicit Makespan variable with a final-position completion bound, and forbids independent per-machine sequences, due dates, release dates, machine-choice, staffing, or unrelated assignment reinterpretations.
